utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that the Stanisic Defence wished to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. May we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Plahuta. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Bakrac will now continue his examination. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day to everyone in the courtroom. Good day, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, last week when we adjourned, do you remember that we had a look prior to adjourning at three documents that related to certain events, -- or, rather, to the action taken by the Drina Corps and the Uzice Corps following the attack launched on Skelani and Bajina Basta. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At the watch-tower at the Perucac dam did you have a map of the area?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had a map. It was necessary in order to see the border area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And on that map -- or, rather, was that map used by your superior to follow the troops' movements, and did you know about where the line was supposed to be, the line where the Uzice and Drina Corps were to link up?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now please have a look at Exhibit 2D1688.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's enlarge the map, first of all, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, here we can see Bajina Basta. And opposite Bajina Basta, Skelani. I don't want to call up the documents we've already had a look at again, but can you see the village of Sase?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the witness a marker so that the witness can mark the location of the Sase village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you mark that location with number 1.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't want to go back to the documents, but we also mentioned the Zeleni Jadar location. Can you see it on the map?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you encircle it and mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you remember where that line was supposed to be, the line where the Uzice Corps fought against Naser Oric's forces, and they were fighting from the east against his forces, and they were to link up with the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the line between the village of Sase, and you bypass Srebrenica and then you link up with Zepa and Luke. That area had to be cut off because it's more elevated that Bajina Basta, and it was, as a result, possible to shell the town on a continual basis, so the line would like this, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, could you tell us something about the forces -- or, rather, the composition, the ethnic composition of the village to the east of this line? Not the forces.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, about 90 per cent of the population of the villages was of Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the documents we've had a look at, the place called Osmace "jezero," Osmace lake, is mentioned. Could you mark that location with number 3, Osmace with number 3, and then could you mark the location of the lake, to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the lake is more or less here in the vicinity of Osmace. That's where this plateau should be in the mountain. It's not very visible, but it would be here, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this map that has now been marked by the witness please be admitted into evidence. And, Your Honour, I also had three documents that I dealt with on Friday, and I would also like to tender them now. I could inform the Registrar of the numbers of these documents so that they can be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. And Madam Registrar is invited to immediately assign a number to them, and we'll then hear from the Defence whether they'll -- from the Prosecution and the Stanisic Defence whether there are any objections. I think first Mr. Bakrac is -- we first take the map which was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Map 2D1688, as marked by the witness, will receive number D854, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document, Your Honour, is 2D1667.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document will receive number D855, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then 2D1670 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... will receive number D856, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And 2D1671, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... will receive number D857, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, since the previous translation continued, I -- the numbers for 2D1670 is not yet on the transcript. Is that D856?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will try to repeat numbers to have it clear on the record. So 2D1667 will receive number D855. The next one was 2D1670 and will receive number D856, Your Honours. And the last one, 2D1671, will receive number D857, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We have no objection to the map being admitted into evidence. With respect to the three documents other than the map, these are part of a Drina Corps collection. These documents were provided to the Prosecution by the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior on December 2004, and we note that they were not on the Simatovic Defence's 65 ter list; however, they all relate to topics covered in the military expert report, which the Simatovic Defence has since withdrawn, and we've thus been able to review the Defence position on relevant issues, so we do not consider the lack of notice to have caused us any prejudice. Therefore, we don't object to the Simatovic Defence adding them to the 65 ter list, using them, or tendering them with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I take it that you'll request the first three documents to be added to your 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You're quite right. And I'd like to thank the Prosecution for not objecting. Yes, they were disclosed to the previous Defence, but that was done recently. I would like to request that these documents be added to our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add the documents which were provisionally assigned numbers D854, 855, and 856, to add it to the Simatovic Defence 65 ter list. D854 up to and including D857 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, since you are part of the Uzice Corps, a member of the Uzice Corps, did you have any knowledge about any victims in the area that you have just marked? And was the area cleaned up?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that there were victims and that hygiene and sanitation measures were taken in the area, and these measures were taken by the Republika Srpska Drina Corps because this is common military practice. If a certain action is being carried out in a certain stretch of the territory, it is for them to take sanitation and hygiene measures. And the victims, as far as I know, were from Naser Oric's forces. They were Serbians --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. You said that victims were, as far as you knew, from Naser Oric's forces. And then you continued. You said they were -- I think you started with, "They were Serbians ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise if I misspoke. The victims that remained on the battle-field were victims who were killed by Naser Oric's forces. What I wanted to say is that the dead were Serbs, and these were the dead who remained as a result of the action taken by his forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, let's have a look at 2D1680. While waiting for that to come up, Mr. Plahuta, this is a document that we received from the Prosecution when they disclosed these documents to us. I think it is a communiqué from the commander of the Uzice Corps. It's addressed to the Drina Corps. And it was sent by Major Dragoljub Ojdanic, the commander of the Uzice Corps. And here it says that the Uzice Corps will continue with its offensive up until the 31st of January, and up to 1200 hours nineteen -- in the year 1993 at the latest. And under item 3, it says that Dragoljub Ojdanic says that it's necessary to have teams for clearing up the battle-field, because in that area there are many bodies. And it is necessary to include journalists in the teams for clearing the battle-field as well as cameramen in order to gather evidence that is necessary for propaganda purposes and in order to document the crimes comitted against the Serbian people. Does this document in fact support what you were saying? Do you have any knowledge according to which this request was made of the Drina Corps by Dragoljub Ojdanic and did the Drina Corps record what he requested?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that is what I was saying. That is correct. I'm not sure whether those teams went into the field and recorded everything, but what is stated here is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could 2D16 please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but why not first get answers to your questions. Do you have any knowledge about this request? That was one of the questions asked. You knew of this request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The command at the watch-tower informed us of the situation in the field in this manner, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you had not seen this document, or did you see this document ever before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I haven't understood you correctly. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document which is on the screen, have you seen this before this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't. I don't think I've ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And did you know anything about Major-General Ojdanic issue this request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure whether the general personally issued that request, but I do know that when the commander at the watch-tower would brief us, would provide us with information, he'd provide us with information of a general kind. He wouldn't say General Ojdanic did such and such a thing, he would say the staff or the command has issued an order requesting that certain things be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You want to tender it into evidence, Mr. Bakrac. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1680 will receive number D858, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is from the same Drina Corps collection of documents referenced earlier, also not on the 65 ter list. But, again, for the same reasons I stated earlier, we would have no objection to adding it to the 65 ter list or its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, same procedure as the previous ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. Could this please be added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I tried to cut it short by saying same procedure. Leave is granted to add it to the Simatovic 65 ter list, and D858 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, last week when we discussed this action that followed the attack on Skelani you said that members of the Uzice Corps, members of the 63rd Parachute Unit, and of the 72nd Special Brigade, and of the Guards Brigade participated in that action; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, if you know, whether any of the units in question sustained losses in the operation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the operation, during the briefing, we were told that the 63rd Air-borne Unit and the units of the Special Corps had sustained losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please look at 2D1639 under seal. I would kindly ask that it not be broadcast publicly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Can I ask that we move into private session to discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In private session. Not only the document to be treated as a confidential document but also go into private session. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have a look at 2D1638 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, in this document, the command of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade in August 1993 requested assistance in the issuance of Red Berets to the 72nd Command of the Special Brigade of the corps of the special forces of the Yugoslav Army. Reference is made to the formation of the Drina detachment of special forces --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: To the Podrinje detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- and some red berets are requested. Do you have any knowledge of this Podrinje red beret detachment having been formed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what its name was, but I know there was a red beret detachment that was formed on the other side of the Drina, in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, in addition to the 72nd Special Brigade, what kind of berets were worn by members of the Guards Brigade and the 63rd Parachute Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had red berets. It was a sign of recognition.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would also like to suggest that this document be added onto our 65 ter list and that it be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And this is from the same collection and our position is the same. We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also not yet on the 65 ter list, if I understand ... yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1638 will receive number D860, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add the document to the Simatovic 65 ter list, and D860 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, was Bratunac also close to Bajina Basta? Is it just on the other side of the Drina river?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is some 50 or 60 kilometres downstream from Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at Exhibit 2D1526. It is an order of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command, signed by Commander Lieutenant-Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The document refers to an order of the Drina Corps command of the 26th of October, 1994, concerning the engagement of the Red Berets Platoon within the MAC-3 operation. It is ordered that the commander of the Red Berets Platoon, Bosko Neskovic, prepare the unit to be introduced into combat in accordance with the previous idea of the MAC-3 operation commander. Mr. Plahuta, on the 27th of October you joined the JATD. My question is this: Do you know Bosko Neskovic, and was he ever a member of the JATD unit of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this name. I don't think he ever was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, you have never met him.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have neither met him nor heard of him. Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would also kindly ask that this document be added onto our 65 ter list and be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection on the basis of authenticity. This document was seized during a mission in Banja Luka. However, the witness hasn't added anything relevant to the document, and in fact, we see from the date that it was well after the time that he was positioned in this area of the Uzice Corps. The Defence could have simply asked him about his knowledge of this person mentioned in the document if that was what they wanted to elicit from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this time in question, according to our information, the witness went from Bajina Basta to Belgrade. My question was whether he had heard of the Red Beret Platoon and whether he knew that Bosko Neskovic ever belonged to the JATD. I think the Prosecution announced that they would have some documents concerning the person in question that they intend to use during their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the witness apparently doesn't know this person mentioned here. What, then, is the probative value of this document? The witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could put whatever document to a witness and say, Do you know the person which is mentioned in this document? And the witness says, No. And then you admit that document into evidence. That's, of course, a bit of a strange way of operating. Best to do is first to ask whether the name is familiar to a witness, and if he says yes, then to put a document in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was our idea in this case -- well, in this case a reconnaissance detachment of the Bratunac Brigade had links established with the Serbian MUP apparently, as alleged here. There is evidence in documents showing that in the area of Bosnia and Republika Srpska there was -- there were a number of Red Beret units that had nothing to do with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia and its state security sector. We wanted to ask this witness, who was a member of the JATD as of October 1994, whether he had ever heard of the person in question who was supposed to be in command of a red beret platoon in the Bratunac area. We wanted to have this document admitted as showing that there were a number of Red Beret units both in Republika Srpska and Croatia which had nothing to do whatsoever with the JATD of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's not what you asked the witness. That's -- but, apparently, there's no objection, or is there an objection, Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We don't object -- we don't dispute the relevance of this document to contentious issues in the case; thus we don't object if the Simatovic Defence would like to tender it from the bar table. However, we would request that if these are the issues that it seeks to elicit from the witness, that it proceed as Your Honours have suggested, asking the witness first before putting documents. And in addition, this last discussion that the Simatovic Defence has put on the record regarding the relevance of the document, if these are issues that it wishes to elicit from the witness, we would ask that other such discussions be made outside of the hearing of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Perhaps why I didn't seek exactly that explanation from Mr. Bakrac, but he gave them. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1526 will receive number D861, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D861, leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter list, and the document is admitted into evidence. Mr. Bakrac, I have one question to you in relation to the previous document, D860. The English translation seems to be of a rather poor linguistic quality. Who translated the document? If, for example, I read that the Zvornik Brigade has formed a maneuver unit, and then it "preformed combat activities in last period of war." I take it that it must be "performed in the last period of the war," but who prepared this translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm checking this with my colleague. I think the translation was uploaded into the e-court system, but, with your leave, if you could allow us some time to investigate the matter, we'll inform you after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have some concerns about the quality. And perhaps the other parties will have a look at it as well, especially those who are native English-speaking persons, because it might be my insufficient knowledge of the English language which caused me to have some doubts. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, before these events in January 1993 in Skelani and Bajina Basta, did you know about Franko Simatovic? Had you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time see him in Bajina Basta, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him, well, I think it was in March 1993, in Bajina Basta in a hotel. Or, rather, it was in front of the hotel. On the terrace of the Drina hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you meet him on that occasion? Did you try to find out who he was?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't meet him on that occasion. But I did ask about who he was, because there were a few of us who were sitting there, and I asked someone, Who is the man in uniform sitting on the other side? And then one of my former colleagues from the watch-tower -- or perhaps he was at the watch-tower at the time, but, in any case, he said that it was Franko Simatovic, an operations officer in the State Security Service. And he said that he had come there in order to set up an electronic surveillance system. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many times did you see him in Bajina Basta during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time? Well, I only saw him on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As a result of the attack on Skelani and Bajina Basta, was any specific action taken? For example, by the MUP of Republika Srpska. And if so, by whom was such action taken?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, security was stepped up along the border, and I also know that a staff, a MUP staff, was set up in the police station in Bajina Basta. And I know that a training camp was set up for the police units. It was a training camp at Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of the MUP staff in Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know which units were under his command?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, it was a MUP staff, and he exercised command over all the MUP forces at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether during that period of time he held the position of the commander of some MUP unit in Republika Srpska -- in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the special police units, the PJM.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that apart from the staff in Bajina Basta there was a camp at the Tara that was established. Do you know who set the camp up?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the camp was set up by Stojkovic, also known as Badza. He set the camp up, that training camp for the special police units, the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now see 2D311. It's a photograph which is on our 65 ter list. While waiting from the photograph to appear on the screen, Your Honours, I would like to say that it's relevant in relation to the descriptions provided by various Prosecution witnesses, the description they provided of Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, could you first tell me whether you can tell where this photograph was taken. Can you identify the location?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. In the background you can see the Drina hotel in Bajina Basta, because it's the only such building in Bajina Basta. It's recognisable. It has lamps of this kind in front of the hotel and trees of this kind as well, so this was a photograph that was taken in front of the hotel in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you said that the hotel is quite specific or recognisable, but you can only see part of the building here.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of the building can be seen. But the whole is what has to be taken into consideration. These lamps surround the hotel. You also have them at the square in Bajina Basta. So these lamps and these trees can definitely be found in front of the hotel in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this what Franko Simatovic looked like when you saw him, as you say, in March 1993 in Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what he looked like. It's a photograph that was quite possibly taken at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And at the time did he wear glasses and did he have long hair?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice that he wore glasses. But as for his hair, yes, he had such hair. Yes, he had long hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could 2D311 please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D311 will receive number D862, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, last week you told us that in April 1993 your contract with the army expired. What did you do after that, and when did you attempt to find a new job within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once my contract with the army had expired, I worked in various private companies, wherever it was possible to earn a little money. And later, I heard that there was a competition. I heard this from colleagues. Bajina Basta is a small town. I heard from someone, from a friend perhaps, that there was a competition, and then I and my later brother went to the police station to register for that competition for the Tara site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you and your late brother registered in the police station in order to undergo some kind of training at Tara. Did you know what sort of unit you were registering for at the time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't know anything about that. All we knew was that it concerned a training centre for the police. As for the unit concerned, we didn't receive any such information in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you and your late brother registered for that competition, what happened after that? Could you briefly tell us.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we registered, they said, Come back in a few days time and we'll tell you about the results. We returned a few days later. They said someone will come to fetch you. You've been accepted in the MUP, someone will come to fetch you, and you will be taken away for training, and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you first tell us when this occurred, in which month and which year?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the month of October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you go to Mount Tara for this training?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In fact, a member of the police force from Tara came to fetch us in a Lada Niva car, and he took four of us to Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which building did he take you to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took us to the so-called Sljivovica hotel on Mount Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who received you there, and how many people or how many men were there involved in the training?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sale received us at Tara. That's how he introduced himself. He didn't tell us his first and last name. He just said he was Sale, a former member of the military. He said that we had arrived at the training centre where training was provided for the MUP, and he said that our training would start on Mount Tara. And he said that later we would see where we would be sent. And there weren't many of us on Mount Tara. There weren't many men. There were about 20 of us, and that included the logistics at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say about 20 with the logistics, there were 20 of you who were attending the course and in addition there was the logistics, or does this include the logistics?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It includes the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So how many of you were involved in the training? How many of you underwent the training?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were the four of us, and with him, that made a total of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Be so kind as to tell us how long this training lasted, and what did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we only did physical exercises on the mountain. We were taught about infantry weapons, and we had to go running, do push-ups, various kinds of physical exercises, and so on and so forth. This lasted for about two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we were told we would be going to the centre in Lipovica. We were also told that it would be a -- that it was a MUP centre, and it's not far from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Lipovica, who received you there? And on that occasion did you learn anything about the unit concerned?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were received by the commander of the base there, Dragoslav Krsmanovic, and he told us that we had arrived at the anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "we," a minute ago you mentioned the four of you who were in Tara, did you go to -- did all four of you go to Lipovica, and was your brother one of the four men?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were the four of us, and naturally my brother was with us, so there were four of us in total, and Sale who had received us on Tara was the fifth person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how much time you spent in Lipovica, and was there any kind of training provided there as well?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the base at Lipovica isn't very big and it is therefore not possible to undergo any kind of serious training. But we also did physical exercises there. We were also taught about various kinds of weapons. We were taught about how to read maps. And that would be it, more or less. We were taught about explosives. So it was a kind of a military training, but it wasn't that intensive. We also performed various logistics tasks. We were still being tested, so to speak. A trial period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many members of the unit were undergoing this training in Lipovica while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were the four of us who were there all the time, but the number of members who were there varied. There were men who had arrived before us, and sometimes men would go home, on leave, they would go to work. So there were up to about 20 men undergoing the training there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there a logistics department at Lipovica, and if so, what did it comprise? Who represented them?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a logistics department at Lipovica. There were quartermasters, caretakers, mechanics, technical personnel, cooks, maintenance workers, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock. Is this a good time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Bakrac. We'll take a break, and we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My apologies for the delay. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before the break, I promised to provide an answer concerning document D860. It was translated by our Defence team, and we sent it to CLSS now for translation. Obviously, our English was insufficient to engage in such kind of translation, and we will do our utmost to correct the mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The leaving out of all the articles in English gave me already the impression that it might be a translator who came from the former Yugoslavia, but there are other -- "performed" and "preformed" is not the same, for example. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac. No, I have one other question for -- I think for D861. I think in the beginning of that document reference is made to some previous decisions on that operation. Is there any way that you could provide those documents to the Chamber as well? You mean, would I -- you see what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I do. I believe I understand what you are aiming at. We will try to gather all documents that we have and the disclosed material and forward it to you concerning the operation mentioned in the introduction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't asking for all documents. I was asking for the two specifically referred to in that heading or in the beginning of this document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Certainly. We'll try to have them located and sent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, before the break we discussed your stay and training at the unit base in Lipovica. Please be so kind and tell us when you arrived there and the date of departure from Lipovica, and where did you go from there? What month and year was that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in Lipovica, as I said, some two weeks following my stay at Tara in early February -- November, 1994. I stayed in Lipovica until end of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll move to that other topic in terms of where you went in late April. But between the period -- or in the period between November 1994 and April 1995, when undergoing the training you have described, did you know who commanded your unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit commander was Meda [phoen] Radonjic. As a matter of fact, he was the assistant of the unit commander because that person had still not been appointed and they were looking for someone with a degree from the military academy, someone of a more senior rank who would act as commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Up until the time you joined the JSO in 1996, was the commander ever appointed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. It was as late as 1996 that they appointed someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us this: You, as someone who had just arrived in the unit and was undergoing training, how were you familiar with that kind of information?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were told by Krsmanovic, I believe. Dragoslav Krsmanovic. When Meda Radonjic came to Lipovica once, we were told that Meda was to come but that he was the assistant commander acting on behalf of the unit commander. We didn't meet him personally because we were lined up and he just passed in front of us. That was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "he passed us by" or "in front of us," who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologies. Medo [phoen] Radonjic, assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned Krsmanovic and Radonjic. While you were at Lipovica from November 1994 to April 1995, did you see anyone else from the Serbian State Security Service in terms of high-ranking officials?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, Milan Tepavcevic, deputy head of the service, arrived. He came a few times, though, but on that occasion I saw him for the first time. We were told that he was deputy head and we had to take care of our equipment, vehicles, and tidy up the entire base because he was a senior official.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know why the deputy head came to the base?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we were engaged in providing logistics at the base, we were in contact with a Milan, Pajser, I think; that was his nickname. He was in charge of a part of logistics concerning the members of the unit and their needs. He told us about Milan, the deputy head of service, that he was the person in charge of equipment, purchasing of assets, and that the unit relied heavily on him. In other words, whatever we received as a unit came through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say Milan, for the record, Milan deputy head, what was his last name?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Tepavcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In Lipovica, between November 1994 and April 1995, did you ever see Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During the same period, did you see Jovica Stanisic at Lipovica?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that you were in Lipovica until late April 1995. Where did you go then, and on whose request or proposal?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late April 1995 I went to Petrova Gora. It was on orders of the then-base commander, Dragoslav Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many of you left and by what means?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- well, two of us went to Petrova Gora, myself and a warehouse employee who was older than me. We were taken there in a Land Rover with a driver, and the vehicle returned to Belgrade after we were dropped off at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you recall the name of the warehouse employee who accompanied you to Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Vulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Once at Petrova Gora, who did you report to and what were your duties?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Petrova Gora, we were received by Milan Karapandza. He awaited us, and he was our superior there throughout our stay at Petrova Gora. We were busy with logistics, because there were a warehouse there. We also had to provide security or stand guard at the Petrova Gora facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by your brother Boris to Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never went to Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From April 1995 until what time were you at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until some ten days before Krajina fell; that is to say, until late July --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: June. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Be so kind and clarify for the transcript: Which month did you mention and which year?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until the end of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Between late April 1995 when you say you went to Petrova Gora and the end of July 1995, how many members of the JATD were there at Petrova Gora, and what duties did they have?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number changed constantly because people went home in Serbia, but it was up to 20, or say between 15 and 20 members of the anti-terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which tasks were you given at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Petrova Gora, I was in charge of the quartermaster's supply -- supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what those supplies included? What was in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was food in the warehouse, some uniforms, boots. There was some infantry ammunition in small quantities for personal use, for rifles and sidearms, and items for personal hygiene, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there another warehouse at Petrova Gora, and if so, who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a warehouse belonging to the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina in the location of the monument at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was in charge of that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all went through the Pauk command. They were in charge. Yes, it all went through them, the Pauk command and Milan Karapandza.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned your duties. Can you tell us what was the duty of the unit members during the time when you were at Petrova Gora? And I mean members of the JATD.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their task was to guard the three facilities, the complex of buildings at Petrova Gora, Magarcevac, and the monument at Petrova Gora. They also had to provide security for the repeater at Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, if you know, what was in the three locations you mentioned where you provided security, and what was the purpose of those facilities?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The facilities housed communications equipment for electronic reconnaissance and the scrambling of signals at all three locations. At Petrova Gora there was an antenna. The same at Magarcevac. And as far as I know, at Pljesevica there was a repeater station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, tell me whether at the Petrova Gora complex there were some other people who provided logistical support, and if so, who were they?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several buildings, including a kitchen with cooks and logistics personnel. There was -- there were two officers of the Pauk command in one of the facilities, and occasionally there were guards at the warehouses from the Pauk command. I believe that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the period between end of April 1995 and end of July 1995, during your stay there, did you see Franko Simatovic at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In what capacity did Franko Simatovic come to Petrova Gora, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. When he arrived with Milan Karapandza, they came to the Petrova Gora facility. We were introduced there, and he told me that he was an operative who was sent to unify the work of people working at the communications systems and technicians, and he was supposed to unify their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me check this to make sure. Who told you that, Franko Simatovic or Milan Karapandza?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Karapandza did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you issue Franko Simatovic with any supplies from the warehouse? And if so, what was it and to what end?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We had a certain quantity of fuel next to the warehouse. It was in barrels. And I filled up the tank of his Land Rover so that he could continue his travel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since he wanted a full tank, do you know where he wanted to go?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that. He wanted to go to the repeater station at Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say you saw him twice or thrice at Petrova Gora in that period. Do you know -- or, rather, do you have knowledge of how long he stayed at Petrova Gora each time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only stayed at Petrova Gora as long as necessary in order to do what he wanted to do with the electronics personnel, and then he would go away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, before we move on to certain lists relating to indemnities. Are you aware of the fact that in the Pauk operation there were also two tactical groups? Two tactical groups participated in that operation.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tactical Group II and Tactical Group III.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who was in command of these tactical groups?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Legija was in command of Tactical Group II and Rajo Bozovic was in command of Tactical Group III.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before you went to Petrova Gora, did you know Legija and Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During your stay at Petrova Gora, did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see Legija or Bozovic during the two-week period you spent on Tara in October 1994, or did you see them in Lipovica during the period of time that you spent there and up until the time that you went to Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said you knew about two tactical groups, Tactical Group II and Tactical Group III. Do you know where the commander of Tactical Group II, which was under Legija's command, was located?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I went to see him on two occasions. I think the command was located in a school or something like that. They had a training centre there for members of Babo's troops. I think it was Babo's Youth. I think they were called the Cherokees or something. They all had these Cherokee haircuts in that centre. As for Tactical Group III, its command was in the town, and it was located in two or three houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: First of all, tell us the following: You said that Tactical Group II, or rather the command of Tactical Group II in the centre, were in a school of some kind. In which town? In which school?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the town of Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said that Tactical Group III had its command which was located in two houses. Which town was that? Where did they have their command, in which town?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was also in Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, to make it clear, Mr. Plahuta, could you tell us who Babo is? You mentioned Babo's Youth? Who went by the nickname of Babo?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Babo was Fikret Abdic's nickname. It was a term of endearment in Cazinska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 2D49, Your Honours, and while we're waiting for it to appear on the screen, the heading says, "National Defence of Western Bosnia Supreme Command Report on the Visit to the Surovi RNC." It seems that the date of the report is the 11th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that is before you arrived then. What I'm interested in is whether this was, in fact, the training centre that Legija was responsible for.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the centre. And they also went by the name of Surovi over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And we can see that in March there were 158 soldiers. Then it mentions the period of training. When you arrived there in April, when you stayed in the training centre, can you tell us how many soldiers there were, roughly speaking, under Legija's command?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the base was full of them, and perhaps the number was even higher than this number that we have here. I think there were even more soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise. My stomach aches a bit. Could I have a brief break to go to the toilet, if it's not a problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone is required to remain standby. We will adjourn for a couple of minutes. --- Break taken at 4.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before I move on to my last question, could 2D49 please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D49 will receive number D863, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, we are discussing two tactical groups; one under Legija and the other under Bozovic. Do you know whether there were members of the JATD from the Republic of Serbia in those tactical groups?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such members.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that the command of Tactical Group III was located in two houses. Do you know what the command consisted of?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that Tactical Group III there were these houses, a group of houses. And as far as I can remember, there was the 1st Detachment of Babo's troops, the 1st Detachment of the Army for the Defence of Western Bosnia. It was called something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: With regard to these tactical groups, II and III, who were they subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were subordinated to the Pauk command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the Pauk command was and who the chief of staff was?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Pauk command was Mile Novakovic, and the chief was Cedo Bolata [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now have a look at P461. This document is under seal, so it shouldn't be broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, we'll first have a look at this list of individuals. The heading says the Republic of Serbia, MUP, RDB, JATD. The date is the 1st of March, 1995, and it says that it is a list of members to be paid daily allowances for the period from the 1st of March until the 15th of March, 1995. Let's now have a look at page 16 of the document. Under number 22 it says Boris Plahuta. Under number 23 it says Dejan Plahuta. Date of engagement: From the 1st to the 15th of March. Where it says Boris, we can see that it hasn't been signed. But next to the name Dejan, there is a signature of some kind. My question is whether you can recognise your own signature here.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you at Petrova Gora from the 1st to the 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where were you between the 1st and 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the Lipovica base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And your brother, Boris, was he at Petrova Gora between the 1st and 15th of March -- from the 1st to the 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't there either. He was also at the Lipovica base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now have a look at the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, on the next and last page of this document, dated the 1st of March, 1995, we can see two names: Boris Plahuta and Dejan Plahuta. Date of engagement: From the 6th to the 30th of November, 1994. Where were you and your brother at that time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of November, well, that's more or less the time when we arrived at the base in Lipovica. Perhaps we arrived a day or two earlier or later, but my late brother and myself were in Lipovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Next to these two names we can see a signature. Is that your signature or your brother's signature?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not my signature nor is it the signature of my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you or your late brother, if you discussed the matter with him, did you ever receive any per diems for the month of November 1994?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, we never received such per diems. I don't know -- but no, we never received any such allowances.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, let's now have a look at something in the same document, which has already been admitted. Let's have a look at page 5. Mr. Plahuta, do you know who Veljko Leka is under number 1?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: A pilot from the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And as for Milorad Stupar and everyone else, can you recognise anyone else in the list?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are two or three other names that I can recognise, but it's a helicopter unit from the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say you can recognise two or three other names. For the record, can you tell us who you recognise as members of the helicopter unit from the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Stupar and Mile Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now have a look at P465.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is also under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, while we're waiting for this document: This document is also a list of members to whom per diems are to be paid, and it concerns the period from the 16th of May to the 31st of May, 1995. Let's first have a look at page 12. Under 1 -- number 1, we have Boris Plahuta, then there's Dejan Plahuta. And the period concerned is the 16th to the 31st of May, 1995. Was your late brother Boris at Petrova Gora from the 16th of May to the 31st of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My late brother was never at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know where he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, he was in the Lipovica base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. Let's now have a look at page 2. It's in the same document. And here we also have a list of members to whom per diems are to be paid, and Radojica Bozovic, is under number 1. We have 28 names in the list. Please have a look at them and tell us whether there are any names that you can recognise. Is there anyone who was a member of your unit for anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there are no members from my unit from the JATD. Not a single member.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 5 now of the same document. Here we have 40 names. Under number 1 we can see the name Milorad Ulemek. Is that Legija?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the names of all 40 individuals, and can you tell us whether there are any members of your unit included in this list?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there are no JATD members in this list either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. Did you know that there were payments of per diems made during your stay at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were payments of per diems, but I don't know who received them and how much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you discuss the per diems amongst yourselves? I mean members of the unit.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Because there were always per diems that were not paid on time, some received it, others did not, or somebody received less. And there was talk of money laundering with relation to the per diems. There were a negative tone to the payment of per diems. They were not paid out in time or some people received them and -- while others did not, so we frequently discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at P468 next.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is also under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, this is a list of members who received per diems during the period between 1 July and 15 July 1995. Let's look at page -- the last page first. Mr. Plahuta, we see Dejan Plahuta and Boris Plahuta. Was Boris Plahuta, your late brother, included in Operation Pauk? And didn't he, indeed, receive the per diems for the period specified?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, he never went to Petrova Gora. He was not at Petrova Gora. As for the per diems, I don't know. I can't recall. But as I said, some per diems were paid while others were not, but he was definitely not with me at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you mentioned Vulic and Karapandza. Can you see them in this list?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 16, Radoslav Vulic. And number 17, Milan Karapandza.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. If we look at the list at page 15, that is to say, the same document at page 15, there is another list. Please have a look at that. Number 1, Mile Mrksic. Have a look at the other names. Can you tell us who these people were?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. Mile Mrksic, as far as I know, he was the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. Tell me this, please: Did you meet some people at Petrova Gora who later on became members of your unit, the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I met Mico Petrakovic, Zoran Gulic, and Dusan Momcilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the transcript, could you be so kind as to repeat slowly the first and last names of the three people you met at Petrova Gora who later on became members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mica [phoen] Petrakovic, Zoran Gulic, and Dusan Momcilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you met them at Petrova Gora, do you know what unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They were with the police of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the SUP in Glina that they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How come you met them at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met them at Petrova Gora through Milan Karapandza. He brought them and introduced them to me, saying that they were policemen subordinated to the Pauk command and that I should issue some fuel to them for their vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you talk to them on that occasion, or did you simply issue them with the fuel?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I simply provided fuel to them, and they just told me that they were going to have lunch at our mess as they were to travel shortly afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you see the three men again after Petrova Gora, and where?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw them again in 1996, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where did you see them, since you say you think you saw them in 1996?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them at the centre in Kula, the base in Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you talk to them on that occasion? Did you inquire how come they appeared in the base in Kula, and what was their business there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk to them much then. We simply recognised each other and recalled when we met and where, and they were applying to be made part of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were they successful in their application?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Following Petrova Gora, where did you go? You say you were at Petrova Gora until late July. What happened then, and where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I went to the Lipovica base and then went home on leave for a few days, some four to five days. After that, I returned to the Lipovica base again and went to Pajzos eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say you went to Pajzos. First of all, when did you arrive at Pajzos, approximately? What month and year, and how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in Pajzos in early August 1995, and I stayed there until December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who sent you to Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in the base in Lipovica, there were about a dozen members who gathered there following their leave. Dragoslav Krsmanovic told us to pack up and go to Pajzos. He accompanied us, I think. We stayed there until the end of the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were you at Pajzos? Where did you go? Is it a facility, and if so, what is it?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a complex at Pajzos. It used to be a winery. There were two or three large wine cellars, there was a Tito's villa, two or three buildings where the members were accommodated. There was a kitchen and a small quartermasters supplies warehouse next to the kitchen. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many members of the JATD were there at the location when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of members changed from time to time. It was up to 20 members at any given time. The accommodation facilities were quite poor and hence no more members could be billeted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What duties and tasks were you assigned at Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our main duty at Pajzos was to provide security for the whole facility at Pajzos. We also did some physical exercise to the extent possible and some training, but that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you guard the winery, or something else? And if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The priority was to guard Tito's villa because it housed electronic equipment for reconnaissance, surveilling, and scrambling. Several operators worked there. From time to time there were also translators there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In addition to you who were there to stand guard, was there any other security for the facility?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing else save for the physical security, the standing of guard that we performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about the entire complex? Was any equipment set up aimed at preventing any incursion?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were mines in the surrounding vineyards so that no one could approach the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Do you know who Boca Medic is?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Skorpions unit and Boca Medic and any knowledge the witness might have about this was not in the 65 ter summary or proofing note for this witness, so we had no notice that this issue would come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, my learned friend is right. I agree. It is my omission. We discussed Arkan and that incident. I am willing to withdraw my question about Boca Medic. It is my omission indeed. We had not announced the Skorpions and Medic, but we did announce the topic of Arkan. When we mentioned that, we omitted to inform the Prosecution about our intent to ask about Medic. In any case, I will withdraw my question if it poses any problems for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: It's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's no need for the Chamber to rule on the matter. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are touching upon a new issue or new area of questioning, then perhaps we better first take the break. Unless you have one or two questions which would easily be dealt with in one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I need between 10 and 15 minutes at the most in order to conclude all together. In any case, we can go on a break. I wasn't sure whether you took into account the brief break we had. In any case, I'll need up to quarter of an hour to conclude. As far as I can see from Mr. Stanisic -- well, it might be a good idea to go on a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since the breaks are always full of work, I think we take and break. And we'll resume at a quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please proceed. Again, I have to apologise, but sometimes there are urgent matters which need to be dealt with during breaks, and I have been hesitant whether or not I should ask my colleagues to sit under Rule 15 bis. But I decided that, although I regret it, that losing eight or nine minutes would be better than to miss most of the session. Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, before the break we were speaking about your stay at Pajzos and your engagement there. From August 1995 until the end of that year, do you know whether Arkan ever visited the complex in Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the beginning of August. I was there when he arrived at Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Arkan arrive on his own, and if not, who accompanied him? And did he enter Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't come alone. He came with his escort. There was one other car, there were seven or eight individuals with him, and he didn't enter Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe the event for us.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the main gate we have the entrance to Pajzos. My brother, in fact, was working at that gate on that day. He was standing guard there. At one point in time he said that he needed help at the gate because only he and another member were there. Several of us who were in one of the buildings went to the gate. He stopped Arkan, naturally informed the operations officer about his arrival at the gate. That was the procedure. And he said that he wanted to enter the Pajzos winery. The operations officer on duty said that he could not enter because there was nothing for him to do there. He had no business there. And then my brother told him that they should go away, they should leave the gate, because there was nothing for them there. He was then very angry and his security got out of the vehicles. He wanted to enter. He didn't provide any reasons for going in. All he did was shout. We did not react to those provocations. Some ten minutes later, having shouted, sworn, and so on and so forth for about ten minutes, he wasn't able to enter. So in the end he turned around and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, your brother was at the gate. He then asked for reinforcements and you were an eye-witness of that event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
