utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have to point your guns at each other, or was there just a discussion?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since the situation was such as it was, we arrived with our weapons, our automatic rifles, and we had our weapons at the ready. We were ready to use them. He saw that. He took that to be a serious threat, and he had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I've understood you correctly, a little earlier on you said that he did not provide any reasons as to why he had appeared. Have I understood you correctly? That's the first question. And if so, did you later find out about the reasons for which Arkan appeared there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since the -- since it was a winery and the cellars hadn't been moved, well, I suppose he may have wanted to take the wine away or perhaps to see whether there was any wine there. So that must have been the reason why he was shouting. He also mentioned the wine. And he even said, What? I want to buy some wine. But in any event, he couldn't go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you remember whether at the time any of your superiors was present? Who from amongst your superiors with you there? And was there anyone in the villa, and if so, who?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the superiors are concerned, at that time Krsmanovic was present there. Dragoslav Krsmanovic. He was up in the villa. And the operations officer on duty probably informed him of the fact that Arkan was there, and he said that he could not go in. That was the chain of command, so he must have done that. And I think there were operators working on these electronic devices in the villa as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While you were at Pajzos from August to the end of 1995, did you see Franko Simatovic there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him arrive on several occasions. I saw him two or three times, and he would go up to the villa. He would go straight there from the gate. There's a path that leads there from the gate, and you could see that he went straight to the villa and he spent some time in the villa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on those two or three occasions when you saw him arriving there, can you tell us how long he would stay there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he would stay there for a lengthy period of time. There were shifts at the gate. But he would spend up to two days in the villa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of speaking to him on such occasions or not?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have the opportunity to speak to him because at the gate we'd just see who it was and then the operations centre would announce him and he would go straight to the villa. We had no contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you said that you stayed at Pajzos until December 1995. Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the December 1995, we went to the centre in Kula. There was a training centre for the anti-terrorist unit that had been set up there, so that's where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you subsequently become a member -- or, rather, at one point in time was the JATD transformed into some other kind of unit? And if so, when?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was transformed into the JSO, the unit for special operations. And this was in August 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you a member of that new unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, was the JSO disbanded at one point in time, and if so, when? And after it had been disbanded, did the unit continue to exist under some other name?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The JSO, the unit for special operations, was disbanded in

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: You wouldn't be wrong. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We can now move back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, do you remember -- in fact, were you present at the unit's celebration in Kula in 1997?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone there? For example, Vasilije Mijovic or Zivojin Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know these two individuals before the celebration in Kula?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know when they arrived? Did they arrive on that day, or earlier on? Did they arrive on the day of the celebration or earlier?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived on the day that the celebration was organised in Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were they in civilian clothing or in uniform?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We have a video here that shows that the individuals I'm asking you about now are in the uniforms -- wearing the uniforms of the unit for anti-terrorist action. You say that they arrived in civilian clothing, but in the film they are in uniform.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The individuals who arrived, several individuals arrived -- in fact, they arrived in civilian clothing and they were issued with the uniforms in our warehouse, and they were given certain insignia that indicated their rank so that they could line up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Plahuta, after that celebration, did you see them in Kula in the unit or anywhere in the vicinity of the unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, when I asked you about Pajzos and the incident with Arkan, I omitted to put a question to you which is as follows: Did you have a warehouse with weapons and ammunition with other materiel and equipment at Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We just had a small warehouse for quartermaster equipment, and this was equipment used for the needs of the unit. We had nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever issue any items from that warehouse to people from the outside, people who weren't members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, I have almost completed my examination. I would now just like to go back to a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P974. And I'd like to see page 13 in the B/C/S version and page 15 in the English version. That's just what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, while we're waiting for the document, it seems to be a document that deals with job specifications within the unit, and it's been discussed at length -- or it was discussed at length before your testimony. You mentioned a certain Milenko whose nickname was Pajser and who worked as an administrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at what we can see under number 37. We don't have the right page yet. It's the 13th page in the B/C/S version and it's page 15 in the English version. It's page 15 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at number 37. And then it says, 21, it says the leader of the group for administrative duties and other duties, Milenko Milovanovic. Is that the administrator whom you called Milenko Pajser?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the documents that I have in front of me are in English. Could I just see the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's not that important, but can you remember the surname?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's Milenko Milovanovic. That would be the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, we spoke about the issue of per diems. Do you know anything about Milenko Milovanovic's fate in the unit? Do you, in fact, know where he worked?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Or up until when he worked there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say up until when he worked in the service. I can't remember. I know he was dismissed from the MUP. It was said that he was dismissed because he'd been stealing per diems from members, because he had those lists on him. He was the person who was, in fact, in charge of those lists for per diem payments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this at the time that the unit was still known as the JATD, or was it once it had been transformed into the JSO?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at the time it was still the JATD.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. Let's now have a look at one more document and I will then have completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the document is 2D1219.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, we can see there's a reference to Republic of Serbia, Serbia MUP, personnel file of the member of the special purposes unit. Are you familiar with this form? Have you ever filled in such a form?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not. I'm not familiar with this form. I have never filled out one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Branko Pavlovic, father's name Milenko, born in Cacak?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the first and last name does not ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is part of a file disclosed to us by the OTP found in Lipovica. We would like to tender it as a separate exhibit. Our Defence asked the Republic of Serbia through its security information agency to provide information about this person, if they have such information in their possession, as to his employment. The answer we received is that the person of this name has no mention in any of their personnel files of either the security agency or the Serbian MUP or the security service of the federal secretariat. They also state that this kind of form was not used when employing people with the RDB. For that purpose, we could look at 2D1219.1. I would also like to tender these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the extent that the Simatovic Defence is -- wishes to tender this document from Branko Pavlovic's personnel file through this witness, it's clear that this witness is not familiar with this form and is not familiar with this person, so there doesn't seem to be any basis to tender this through the witness. And the Defence has further offered its own submissions about a response that it received from Serbia which we would submit is also not evidence. So I'm not sure what probative value that would have. If Defence wishes to tender this from the bar table, we recognise, based on their submission, that the argument that they wish to make and the reason that they would wish to tender it, and we would request that the entire file be tendered rather than this mere excerpt. We have a translation ready of this entire file if the Court rules that this can be admitted as such. The Defence is relying on this single page of Branko Pavlovic's personnel file; however, there is little probative value in taking this card alone, completely out of context. Whereas taken as a whole, the documents in Mr. Pavlovic's file indicate that he joined the unit in August 1991 as a volunteer of the RSK MUP; then in November 1991, moved into a special --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you. Apparently you are quoting what -- a document which you would like to have in evidence. Now, that's not the usual way, that you first read to us and then ask whether to have it in evidence because then you've put it on the record. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, the Chamber disagrees with you that the witness couldn't tell us anything about this form. Perhaps not specifically for this person but that apparently this form was not used when he became a member of the service. That, at least, adds something. How much is still to be evaluated, but adds something to just tendering the document from the bar table. At the same time, to the extent that there's a suggestion in it that these forms did not really relate to what happened in the service but that it must be wrong or whatever, if you would seek to sender the remainder of it to put -- give context to this, then we would wait and see whether you do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's absolutely our position. We would not object to the entire file being admitted; whereas we object to simply this excerpt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: -- being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't it not be appropriate that Mr. Bakrac is focussing very much on this form and the witness saying, I'm not aware that it was used, it was at least not used in respect of myself, to leave it for this moment to that? And if you want to tender the rest in cross-examination, you may have an opportunity to tender that. And then we'll decide on that request.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's -- I leave it in Your Honour's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: At the same time, the witness did say he's not familiar with this person, so it would just be a matter of putting a file of someone unfamiliar to him, to him. But I leave it in Your Honours' hands. If that's ... whatever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's also about the form used which was not used in respect of him as a member of the ... so that goes a bit beyond. I would agree if that question would not have been asked. But it was asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned to the document would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1219 will receive number D864, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Does it have to be under seal? Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't see -- well, perhaps the OTP could be of assistance. I think it should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this excerpt is actually from the redacted files, so this particular excerpt does not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's then a public document. Mr. Bakrac, that was your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, I would kindly ask for your decision concerning 2D1219.1, which is the response of the Republic of Serbia concerning this form and the person in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't -- we object to admission of this document. It hasn't been put to the witness and the witness hasn't been given an opportunity to comment on it. And even so, we submit that it has low probative value and is essentially an unexamined -- uncross-examined statement by someone in the Serbian government who in turn summarises a letter from BIA; thus we see no reason that it should be admitted. We object to its admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, my intention was simply a practical one, to have it introduced through this witness. The witness, of course, is unfamiliar with the document, and I agree. But then the option is to have it bar tabled. I was led by practical reasons, because we went back to the security information agency concerning the file, the forms, and the person in question; therefore, it is for you to rule on, but I can also submit it in the absence of any witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you oppose a bar table submission?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, we would oppose the bar table submission. Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A number will be assigned to it provisionally. We'll mark it for identification and we'll think about it. And perhaps you might think about it after we've heard whether the Prosecution wants to tender more of this same personnel file. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1219.1 will receive number D865, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just inquiry, please, whether the Prosecution -- we're searching our records, but we've got no record that the Prosecution have disclosed a translation of this file, so we're anticipating about 17 [Realtime transcript read in error "70"] new files, only two of which have got translation. So we are getting deeply concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will make sure that the translation of this one is disclosed immediately if it has not been disclosed already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then for the follow-up, it's not marked for identification. Is -- are we talking about the personnel file? Or ... No, we are talking about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The -- the file that we were just discussing, the Pavlovic. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- I think the record said -- says I stated "70 new files," and I said "17." I think that we're going to see that during the Prosecution's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Harbour has raised an expectation that you would find the translation soon, Mr. Jordash. I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. This is uploaded as 65 ter 6499, and this was on the list of documents that we noticed for use on cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Bakrac, you are done?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was on my feet because I wanted to thank the witness and you and to say that I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I said something about losing nine minutes. You lost 13 or 14, Mr. Bakrac. Let's move on. Mr. Jordash, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apologies. I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just want to pick up very quickly on the issue of Arkan coming to Pajzos. A witness in this trial claimed a number of things about Arkan or Arkan's Men coming to Pajzos. First of all, he claimed that when Arkan's unit needed supplies, they would come to Pajzos and, as a routine, be supplied by Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's JF-048, P523.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know if they took anything from Pajzos. First of all, we did not have a large warehouse. We didn't have the quantities of equipment needed to issue to anyone. That's one thing. Another thing: I can guarantee that during my stay there they did not come there and we did not supply them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he claimed that three to four crates of ammunition and uniforms were given to Arkan by Dragan Garic. Can I take it you have no knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He later contradicted himself and stated that Arkan's Men had come on only one occasion that he'd seen. Did anyone ever tell you that Arkan had been supplied, whether frequently or just the once, by Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I ask you the same about Boca, the commander of the Skorpions. JF-048 also claimed two things: One, that Boca were supplied frequently; and then later he retreated from that and said Boca's men, he was aware, had been supplied once.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that's, Your Honours, P523 and P5767.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to cast any light on that, whether Boca's men were once or a number of times supplied by Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said before, he did not come there and we did not have enough ammunition or equipment to issue it to anyone. As far as I know, neither Boca nor any of his men came there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask for clarification of that last exhibit that Mr. Jordash referred to. P5767 appears not to be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps he intended to refer to a transcript page, because that number is within the range of the transcript where Witness JF-048 testified. But looking at that transcript, Mr. Jordash, I have not yet found -- 5767 is the first page of Wednesday, the 16th of June, 2010, and seems not to reflect any testimony whatsoever of a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I should have said -- Your Honour's right, it's page 5856 of the transcript. And what I can do is set this out a bit more clearly. P523, the Witness JF-048 said that when Arkan's unit or Boca's unit needed supplies, they would come to Pajzos with requisite permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the transcript page number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I do beg your pardon. Its page 5805 to page 5807. I'm sorry. I put this together very quickly just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because you again refer to a first page of a session. Apparently where --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll have a look, because now I'm going to check it carefully, whether we find ... I found the relevant pages. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's just return, then, to this issue of Arkan coming and being turned away. You said today at transcript page 50 that "He had no business there. All he did was shout." And at page 51, that Krsmanovic was there. Why wasn't he invited in to chat with Krsmanovic or someone else about what he wanted?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As guardsmen at the gate, we were in contact with the duty operations officer who was in charge of communicating with the guards and the communications centre in the villa and the people there. We turned to him and he simply told us to ask him to remove himself, that he was not allowed to enter. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Why? Why would -- do you know why the guardsmen refused to let him enter? Was there a specific reason communicated to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not a reason. We were simply told that he had no business there. And we were doing our job. We were guarding our communications facility. No one could approach it unless they have an approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, did I miss this? Who was the guardsman? Sorry, no. Who was the duty operations officer?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty operations officer could have been either a group leader or any of the 20 of us who were guarding the facility. That person was in charge with communicating with the centre up in the villa as well as with the guardsmen at the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But what I'm trying to get at is that Arkan was given such, on one view, discourteous treatment, i.e., told to go away, he had no business there, and I want to know whether that's because the person making the decision didn't like Arkan, or it was known within Pajzos that Arkan wasn't welcome. What was the understanding about Arkan being sent away, the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no particular reason. He was refused entry as would any other person unauthorised to enter. There was no need for a specific reason to be refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was it only those who were connected to, engaged by, or employed by the DB who were allowed to enter?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only people who could enter were members of the JATD and operatives, the technical personnel manning the electronic equipment, as well as those who worked in logistics. No one else could enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, last week you started off your evidence by -- your evidence concerning your engagement in Bajina Basta by saying that in September 1992 there was some sort of competition for contractor soldiers -- for professional soldiers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's, Your Honours, page 19309.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was around that time. In September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you just elaborate on that? Am I correct that at this time those men, such as yourself, who had not been conscripted into military or MUP forces would answer calls from various military formations or MUP forces and go and work as contract soldiers? Was this a common phenomena, as you saw it, at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time it was enough -- well, I mean, civilians, simple members who were not older than 28 and who had served a military term, any such people could apply for a position of contract or professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I have, please, on the screen P392.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a comment or an entry in a diary or notebook kept by Mladic. While that's coming on the screen, are you able to give any idea or clue concerning the number of men who were registering as contract soldiers at Bajina Basta at the time you did, around September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, quite a lot of men had registered. I don't remember the exact number now. But in that area of the Drina, the watch-towers and the so-called dry borders were occupied by contract soldiers or covered by contract soldiers. So there were quite a few such men.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, page 37. I think it should be the next page. Page 2 of this document, but page 37 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, this is a notebook kept by Mladic, and I would just want to ask if this is the type of contracting that we're talking about. Mladic notes that he had a meeting with political structures in Doboj, 6th of February, 1993. They pointed out: "1. Major problems with various backroom dealings from," perhaps, "Ozren." And then 2: "Lazarevic ... now called Ciganovic, lives in Belgrade and has permission from Stanisic to form the Red Berets at Ozren (Mico wrote an order from Bozovic to form a special unit at the SJB in Doboj), and these units would serve to drain natural resources from this area." Were you aware that Bozovic was a contract soldier around this time who had come to an agreement with Mico Stanisic? Did you become aware of that at any time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. It's not based on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could my learned friend clarify that, please? I am not sure of the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The document does not say anything about contract soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. It said Mica was ordered -- or received an order -- I beg your pardon, Bozovic received an order to form the Red Berets in Doboj, that order by Mica Stanisic. And it's our case that that's precisely what happened, and Bozovic was a contract soldier. So I asked the witness about the document, and the question was based on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a -- the objection is denied. You may -- the witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of somebody called Slavko Lazarevic who was somebody, perhaps, who was arranging contract soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard of that name, Slavko Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of Bozovic at this point in time in early February, or the first six months of February at least, working for the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the MUP of the Republika Srpska? No, that's some sort of a mistake. I didn't work for that MUP. I worked for the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, I think there's been a problem with my question. I'm asking whether you heard or knew that Bozovic was working for the RS MUP at this point in time. Not you.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on, then. Now, I want to ask you about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the expression "RS MUP" is asking, of course, for problems, because does it stand for Republic of Serbia or does it stand for Republika Srpska? Which --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You're right. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, that's asking for problems. So if you would please always be clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just so you're clear, Mr. Witness, I was talking about the Republika Srpska MUP. Did you take my question in that way?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, you asked me whether I was aware of the fact that Bozovic worked for the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's what I asked.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Let's move on to the operation in Skelani. Now, the -- I want to try to make sure we understand what this was all about, and I want to focus, first of all, on the role and the contribution of the military from Serbia - in particular the special unit, the 68th Guard Brigade, 72 -- 72nd Special Brigade, and the 63rd Parachute Brigade - and then later, tomorrow, I want to ask you about the role of the Serbian MUP. So before we begin looking at these two different formations, I want to understand precisely what the operations in Bosnia, around Skelani, were focussed upon. It's correct, isn't it, that around 16th of January, 1993, Skelani had been taken over by Muslim forces? Correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's correct that - let me try not to exaggerate - but is it -- would you say -- would you agree with this, that thousands of Serbians had fled into Serbia from the villages in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the villages along the Drina had been torched and burnt and civilians killed and atrocities comitted along and around the Skelani municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The attacks which had taken place in the Skelani municipality had not been limited to Skelani but had also been aimed and directed at settlements within Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: From what you knew from your involvement, is this fair, what a witness in this court said, Milovanovic, the deputy to Mladic, on the 7th of December, 2011, page 15410 said that as: "If people in those villages along the Drina within Bosnia heard shots 20 kilometres away, Serbs would immediately flee across the Drina into Serbia." So apart from the attacks by Oric's men, would you agree with that testimony, that it was a common occurrence, effectively, for Serbs to flee from the Serbian villages along the Drina into Serbia, trying to avoid attack?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: In villages further away from the border, they would flee from those villages from the territory in Skelani on the Bosnian side. And when there was an attack, all those who could flee to Serbia would do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, was it clear to you at the time you were contracted in the way that you testified that the objective of the forces from Serbia, the special brigades we've mentioned, was to push the Muslim forces back from those burnt villages to allow Serbs to return to their villages? Was that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They had to cross over because that part of eastern Bosnia is more elevated. They had to enter the territory in order to defend the Serbian villages and the town of Bajina Basta in order to prevent it being shelled from more elevated positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. Could you please find a last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: On that last point, I want to be very clear about what I'm asking you so that we're clear about your answer. I'm nothing talking about what the VRS may have been doing before Oric's attacks, whatever their objectives were within Bosnia. I'm talking about when those specials brigades from Serbia became involved within Bosnia. It's clear to you, isn't it, that their involvement was triggered by Oric's men coming and brutalising those Serbian villages?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA: [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have understood your question correctly, you are asking me when these special forces from Serbia became involved and had to cross over the bridge and enter the territory of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And trying to pinpoint exactly what, in your mind, was the trigger for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you've asked that, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll resume this tomorrow, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may resume that tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because otherwise we'll finish too late. We adjourn for the day. But I would first like to instruct you, Mr. Plahuta, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with anyone about your testimony, whether testimony already given or still to be given. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 this same courtroom. Already any indication as to how much time you would need, Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Approximately three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any estimate about how much more time you would need, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: An hour and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An hour and 45 minutes. We adjourn. And we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 15th of May, 9.00 in morning in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
